comparison: Perfect agreement on proteomic interaction data (C13-C15, C35-C39). Both evaluations find the co-immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry evidence convincing and well-controlled. OpenEval emphasizes methodological details while peer reviewers highlight alignment with prior findings.

Strong agreement on ChIP-seq data quality and findings (C40-C46). Both find the genome-wide localization data convincing. Peer review includes C18 in their evaluation while OpenEval focuses on the specific ChIP-seq claims. Both accept the evidence for subtelomeric recruitment and distinct binding patterns.

Agreement on PfMORC co-localization with ApiAP2 factors (C47-C50). Both evaluations accept the overlap analysis and motif enrichment findings. Peer review additionally includes C89 (broader integration claim) while OpenEval appropriately notes the data cannot distinguish single vs. multiple complexes.

Complete agreement on chromatin mark co-localization analysis (C51-C53). Both evaluations accept the evidence for inverse correlation with H3K36me2 and lack of co-localization with other tested marks. No concerns raised by either evaluation.

Divergent evaluations of RNA-seq knockdown data (C16-C17, C56-C57, C60-C61, C83). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with acknowledgment of incomplete knockdown limitations. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, expressing concern that 50% knockdown makes it difficult to interpret PfMORC's role in chromatin architecture vs. gene expression.

Agreement on var gene and hypervariable gene family findings (C62-C64, C84). Both evaluations accept the RNA-seq evidence for downregulation of these gene families. OpenEval notes interpretation limitations with non-recloned parasites while peer reviewers accept the findings as valuable insights.

Partial overlap with divergent evaluations. OpenEval addresses C65-C66 (minimal ChIP/RNA-seq overlap and chromatin structure inference) as SUPPORTED. Peer review addresses overlapping claims (C65-C66, C19, C74, C90-C91) as UNCERTAIN, noting that 'direct functional outcomes remain an inference' and expressing concern about the partial knockdown approach.

Agreement on glmS knockdown methodology (C54-C55). Both accept the 50% reduction as established in prior work. However, peer reviewers note this as a limitation for interpreting results while OpenEval treats it as appropriate justification for experimental conditions.

Agreement on melatonin independence findings (C87-C88). Both evaluations accept the minimal overlap between melatonin-induced DEGs and PfMORC-KD DEGs. Peer reviewers implicitly accept by not challenging; OpenEval explicitly supports with qualification about 'at most a minor role.'

Partial overlap with divergent evaluations. OpenEval addresses integrated multi-omics conclusions (C19, C73-C74, C89-C91) as SUPPORTED with appropriate qualifications. Peer review addresses subset of these claims (C19, C74, C90-C91) as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing that functional outcomes remain inferential.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding drug target claim (C92). Both evaluations rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes the claim requires considerations beyond the study's scope (druggability, toxicity, resistance). Peer reviewers express concern that functional outcomes remain inferential and partial knockdown limits understanding.

Agreement on PfMORC essentiality from prior work (C21-C22). Both evaluations accept this background claim supported by citations to prior studies. OpenEval includes broader context (C20, C23) while peer review focuses specifically on essentiality.
